requirements.requirement: VyOS node1 routes Kubernetes traffic bidirectionally between lan-a and lan-b.
requirements.summary: Node1 was configured with gateways on both private LANs. Direct route lookups and pings succeeded in both directions, and the saved configuration and reachability recovered after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Node2 is the Ready control plane, while node3 and node4 are Ready workers.
requirements.summary: The final recovered state shows node2 Ready with the control-plane role and node3/node4 Ready as workers. Their InternalIPs are respectively 10.100.177.11, 10.100.228.11, and 10.100.228.12, and every system and test pod is Ready and Running.

requirements.requirement: Kubernetes control and data traffic uses the private LANs rather than the management network.
requirements.summary: Workers joined the API at the private node2 endpoint. Final node InternalIPs are private, Flannel actively selects enp8s0, and live routes and VXLAN peers use only 10.100.177.x and 10.100.228.x addresses; no 10.100.153.x management address appears in observed Kubernetes node or overlay-peer state.

requirements.requirement: Pods communicate across lan-a and lan-b.
requirements.summary: After all node restarts, a pod on node2 directly fetched the expected payload from pod IPs on both node3 and node4. Live Flannel forwarding entries also identify the private worker and control-plane addresses as overlay peers.

requirements.requirement: Cluster DNS and ClusterIP services work across the cluster.
requirements.summary: The final post-restart checks resolved the test service to its ClusterIP, fetched its expected content through that service, and resolved kubernetes.default from a lan-b pod. Both CoreDNS replicas and all related workloads were Ready.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The supplemental restart protocol is also complete for every managed node: each sequence includes healthy pre-state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity, and recovered routing, services, workload data, and cluster state (node1: cmd-fc5bf3c1d4534370, cmd-669de68a1dd441ee, cmd-3a02c657fdd5471d, cmd-99862b29777d46b8, cmd-c7254d68d0bc46b2; node2: cmd-cb11ea2ddc6d4ccc, cmd-4c67d2a8f6fe4ab4, cmd-267fc412bedd444a, cmd-5ea7900388ce44bd, cmd-5026f33ef07144fa, cmd-09c90fa808d84b5f; node3: cmd-97297f50ea5c4f16, cmd-b0de5bce3a8e4e5e, cmd-6dba0cacc49b4ee3, cmd-94a6582389fd49f9, cmd-26e36d95c295458b; node4: cmd-1efb6794e280434f, cmd-8ca890c304004660, cmd-c9a640c8a968402a, cmd-efef58b9124148cf, cmd-deae0889a5c441a2, cmd-83a17ae83438457b). The fixed before/after boot observations independently corroborate all four identity changes.
limitations: Management-network exclusion was not verified with packet capture or flow counters. Active interface selection, routing, node addresses, and VXLAN peers demonstrate that observed Kubernetes traffic uses the private LANs, but wildcard listeners in global:after_executor:node2:listening-sockets, global:after_executor:node3:listening-sockets, and global:after_executor:node4:listening-sockets do not prove firewall-level inaccessibility from management.

The pre-change VyOS firewall state was not captured because cmd-ae72557f28d44abe failed before configuration was displayed. Therefore, the effective exposure delta of the global forward default-action accept set by cmd-67904f6a1eb34385 is indeterminate and was not assumed to be an unnecessary security weakening.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations directly established routing, Kubernetes prerequisites, the cluster, bounded functional evidence, or mandatory restart evidence. Two low-risk unnecessary retained changes are visible: kubectl was installed on node3 and node4 and later placed on hold despite never being used on either worker (cmd-34b85e42a4374bd0, cmd-d43dcce22c114f5a, cmd-b3278079bea54788, cmd-e88a0bc1230c4f36); and the validation-only client pods created with a 365-day sleep remained Running after testing (cmd-fdcf2c8b5bcb452d, cmd-5026f33ef07144fa). Neither was reverted. The failed package configuration was repaired, the bootstrap token was deleted, temporary installer files disappeared across the required restarts, package health was clean, and no failed services remained. The test web deployments and ClusterIP service are treated as task-relevant demonstrations rather than residue.
